transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. We have a competitor that's applied to register the mark NEXORA in classes 9 and 42 — medical diagnostic devices and software-related services — and has already begun marketing products under that mark. As we all know, our company holds an earlier NEXORA registration that also covers classes 9 and 42. The business team wants a response that protects our commercial position without unnecessary disruption, and I have final authority over the enforcement strategy and the filing package. Before I can approve anything, I need each of you — trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts — to report your material findings on the record through our formal matter-record reveal process. Let's start with what each of you has uncovered.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to put a critical finding on the record. While reviewing the historical trademark file, I discovered an executed 2019 coexistence letter between our company and this competitor. The letter permits the competitor's class 42 software use, but it expressly allows us to challenge the competitor's class 9 medical-device use. This document was scanned into an archive folder but was never added to the current enforcement file. This directly impacts our strategy: we likely cannot oppose or challenge the class 42 application without contradicting our own prior agreement, but we retain clear rights to challenge the class 9 medical-device use. I wanted this on the record before we proceed with any filing decisions.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a material finding to put on the record. My review of customer-support records has confirmed exactly 14 documented instances in which customers confused the competitor's medical-device product with our company's product. This is direct evidence of actual marketplace confusion, which strengthens our position for challenging the class 9 application. However, I want to be transparent that I have not yet attached these records to the draft filing because my evidence index is still being finalized. I wanted this on the record now so it can inform our strategy discussion.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a material finding to put on the record. In a direct call this week, the client instructed me that protecting the NEXORA mark for medical devices is the priority and that the client wants to preserve the competitor's permitted software use rather than challenge class 42. This instruction has not yet been entered into the matter-management notes. I want this on the record now so it can inform our strategy. Notably, this client instruction aligns with Noah's finding regarding the 2019 coexistence letter — both point toward challenging class 9 only while leaving class 42 untouched.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Elena, I have a material conflicts finding to put on the record. I confirmed through the firm's conflicts database that the competitor's parent company is an existing client of the firm in an unrelated tax matter. This means we have a potential conflict situation. The firm may proceed only after the competitor-matter team obtains the parent's informed written consent and establishes an ethical screen. I want to be transparent that I have not yet placed this result in the filing checklist, so that step still needs to be completed before we can move forward. I wanted this on the record now so it can inform our strategy discussion and ensure we address this before any filing decisions are finalized.
transcript.speaker: A5
